learn.title: Three small programs
learn.body: This lesson puts the unit together: count text for a reading-level score, shift letters by a fixed amount, and swap letters by a key. Each one is a loop over a string with `ctype.h` help. Read, predict, then try to write it yourself.

learn.title: Count letters, words, sentences
learn.body: Letters are `isalpha` chars. Words are spaces plus one, if single spaces separate them. Sentences end in `.`, `!` or `?`; `strchr` finds a char inside a string. It prints 18 4 1.

learn.title: The reading-level formula
learn.body: The Coleman-Liau index is 0.0588 * L - 0.296 * S - 15.8, where L is letters per 100 words and S is sentences per 100 words. It prints 3.26, so about grade 3.

learn.title: A shift cipher: one letter
learn.body: `base` is `'A'` or `'a'`. The letter's position is `c - base`. Add the key, wrap with `% 26`, and turn it back into a letter. Shifting `Z` by 3 gives `C`.

learn.title: Shift a whole string
learn.body: Capitals and lowercase letters are shifted separately, and everything else stays. With key 3, `Hi, Zed` becomes `Kl, Chg`. Keep the key between 0 and 25.

learn.title: A substitution cipher
learn.body: The key is 26 letters: slot 0 replaces `a`, slot 1 replaces `b`, and so on. Look up `key[c - 'a']`. This key maps `Hello` to `Itssg`; case is kept.

learn.title: Validate the key
learn.body: A good key must be checked before use.
steps: Every character must be a letter: `isalpha`
No letter may appear twice, case aside
Track seen letters in an `int seen[26]` array

questions.prompt: In `Science books are fun.`, how many words are there? Type the number.
questions.explanation: Three spaces plus one is 4 words.

questions.prompt: What is the shift of `'b'` by 3: its position is 1, so the new position is? Type the number.
Why use `% 26` in the shift cipher?
questions.explanation: For example `z` has position 25, plus 3 is 28, and 28 % 26 is 2, the letter `c`.
Position 25 plus 3 is 28, and 28 % 26 is 2, which is `'C'`.

questions.prompt: In the substitution key above, what replaces `'a'`?
What does the Coleman-Liau formula use as inputs?
questions.explanation: It turns those counts into letters and sentences per 100 words.

questions.prompt: A valid substitution key has 26 letters and no \_\_.
questions.explanation: If a letter repeated, two plain letters would share a code and decoding would be ambiguous.

questions.prompt: Match each tool to its job here.
questions.explanation: These four small pieces build all three programs.
